title: Glossary
description: Terms used across the OmniSign documentation.

terms.definition: The ETSI standard for embedding advanced electronic signatures in PDF documents. OmniSign implements its four baseline levels: B-B, B-T, B-LT and B-LTA.
The European Commission's open-source library for creating and validating eIDAS-conformant signatures. OmniSign performs all signing, validation and timestamping through it.

terms.abbreviation: electronic IDentification, Authentication and trust Services
terms.definition: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market. It defines qualified signatures, trust service providers, and the trusted lists that validation resolves against.
The European standards body whose specifications define the PAdES signature levels, the trusted-list format, and the validation policy and report formats OmniSign uses.
The European Commission's root list, pointing at each member state's national trusted list. Validation walks it to decide whether a certificate belongs to a qualified trust service.
An organisation issuing certificates, timestamps or other trust services under eIDAS. A member state's trusted list enumerates its providers and the services each one offers.
A trust service that issues RFC 3161 timestamp tokens. OmniSign contacts one to add the signature timestamp of B-T and the archival document timestamp of B-LTA.
A trust service that issues digital certificates, binding a public key to a named subject. Validation walks a signature's certificate chain up to a CA it can trust through a trusted list.
The base PAdES level: a basic electronic signature with no timestamp. It is verifiable only while the signing certificate and its revocation data are still available.
The PAdES level that adds an RFC 3161 signature timestamp, fixing the moment the signature was made independently of the signing certificate's own clock.
The PAdES baseline level that adds certificate revocation data (CRL or OCSP) to a timestamped signature, so it stays verifiable once the signing certificate has expired.
The PAdES baseline level that adds an archival document timestamp on top of B-LT. Renewing that timestamp before its own algorithms or certificates weaken keeps the signature verifiable indefinitely.
A signed list, published by a certificate authority, of the certificates it has revoked before their expiry date.
A protocol for asking a certificate authority about the revocation status of a single certificate, instead of downloading a whole revocation list.
The standard interface to a cryptographic token. OmniSign loads a vendor library to sign with a smart card or USB token, so the private key never leaves the device.
A password-protected file (.p12 or .pfx) holding a private key together with its certificate chain. OmniSign can sign from one directly, without a hardware token.
Authenticating once against a central identity provider and reusing that session elsewhere. The OmniSign server supports it through OIDC, or by trusting headers injected by an authenticating proxy.
An identity layer built on OAuth 2.0. The OmniSign server can delegate sign-in to an OIDC provider and issue its own session token afterwards.
A signed, self-contained token carrying claims about its bearer. The OmniSign server issues HMAC-signed tokens to represent an authenticated session.
A lightweight, text-based data format. OmniSign can export a validation report as JSON for machine processing.
A structured, text-based markup format. OmniSign exports the DSS and ETSI validation reports as XML, and builds custom trusted lists as ETSI TS 119 612 XML.
An unstructured plain-text file. OmniSign can export a human-readable validation report as plain text.
